notes: Endpoints are limited to operations directly supported by the authoritative data model and query patterns.

No write/update endpoint is defined for execution_requests or rule_execution_logs because the source of truth for ingestion is asynchronous queue/API ingestion in the existing system, and no authoritative query pattern was provided for runtime write APIs.

Retention purge execution is represented only as a preview/list endpoint backed by QP13 plus an administrative purge trigger using straightforward deleteMany CRUD implied by the data model; no archival endpoint is defined because archival is explicitly an open question/out of scope for the POV.
Authorization details are out of scope for the data model, but endpoints that expose detailed logs are intended for admin/authorized roles only per FR9.

backend_architecture":"A practical backend for this contract can be implemented as a small set of feature-oriented modules over MongoDB. An API layer exposes the REST endpoints and performs request validation, auth checks, and customer scoping. A customer-config module handles GET/PUT of customer logging settings against the customers collection. A request-audit module implements request summary lookup, correlation-ID lookup, request listing, rule-trace retrieval, full drill-down retrieval, JSON-path search, and custom extracts by composing QP1, QP3, QP4, QP5, QP7, and QP11. A rule-execution-search module serves deep troubleshooting searches over rule_execution_logs using QP2 and QP6. An analytics module owns the three aggregate-report endpoints backed by QP8, QP9, and QP10, including safe mapping of dimensionName path parameters to allowed analytics_dimensions fields before building the aggregation pipeline. A retention module supports operational lifecycle management: one service previews purge candidates using QP13, and another executes administrative deleteMany operations on execution_requests and rule_execution_logs for confirmed purge cutoffs. Under these feature modules, a repository/data-access layer should encapsulate the exact MongoDB find/findOne/aggregate/deleteMany/updateOne calls so endpoint handlers remain thin and traceable to the named query patterns. Cross-cutting middleware should enforce authorized access to detailed log endpoints per customer role configuration, validate date ranges and dynamic JSON paths, and attach customer context so every query is scoped by customer_id as required by the data model and single-tenant deployment assumptions."}大发官网 to=functions.ApiContractDesignOutput 《凤凰大参考json  天天中彩票买ByValidator{
